newsitem.title: FRANCE: British Airways takes over Air Liberte operations.
newsitem.headline: British Airways takes over Air Liberte operations.

text.p: British Airways took control of insolvent French carrier Air Liberte on Monday when Air Liberte's board appointed a BA official as its new chairman.
Air Liberte said in a statement that the board elected Marc Rochet, chairman of British Airways' French subsidiary TAT, as its new head on Monday after founder Lotfi Belhassine resigned.
"This is just a formality while we await the court's decision," a spokeswoman for Air Liberte said.

A commercial court in Creteil near Paris is expected to formally approve a rescue plan proposed for Air Liberte by British Airways and its French partner Banque Rivaud on January 8 after consultations with Air Liberte's creditors.
In November the court decided not to liquidate Air Liberte, which went into receivership in September, clearing the way for a takeover by BA and Rivaud.

Despite criticism of foreign takeovers of French companies, the BA/Rivaud plan has been widely expected to win the court's approval, as prospective rivals such as Virgin Express declined to put in bids.
Under the plan, BA would take a 70 percent stake and Rivaud 30 percent in the airline. The plan aims to make Air Liberte break even by 1999 and preserve 1,250 of the 1,400 jobs.
It offers creditors a small percentage in cash immediately or the entire amount of nearly one billion francs ($190.5 million) over 10 years.
"Mr Marc Rochet said he was determined to work as hard as possible for the recovery of the company," Air Liberte's statement said.
Rochet previously said that BA planned to merge TAT and Air Liberte, both of which are losing money but which have a combined 22 percent of the French market.
Air Liberte, which owns a quarter of the landing and take-off slots at Paris's Orly airport, went into receivership after running up 650 million francs in losses in the first nine months of the year.
The carrier was battered by a fare war that erupted after the domestic market was liberalised at the start of 1996 to prepare the industry for full competition in Europe next year.
The French market is dominated by Air France's regional carrier Air France Europe, formerly known as Air Inter.
BA and Rivaud teamed up to make a joint offer in October after Rivaud fell out with its previous bidding partners, which included Air Maroc and travel group Nouvelles Frontieres.
BA originally offered to buy Air Liberte for 25 million francs and pledged 440 million francs in investment but amended its proposal to submit a joint recovery plan with Rivaud.
It moved to block French airline AOM, part of the doubtful Credit Lyonnais assets grouped in the state enterprise CDR, from launching a rival offer by appealing to Brussels.
The path was cleared for British Airways earlier this month after Richard Branson's Virgin Express said it would not bid for Air Liberte as it viewed the operation as too costly.
